cards.title: Work from Home for BPO / KPO and Contact-Centre Agents (v4, 14 slides): Virtual Desktops for Contact-Centre Apps plus the Turbo UDP Tunnel for VoIP
cards.client: An Indian bank running five contact-centre locations on an Android VoIP app, bringing around 500 agents online from home
cards.key_problem: Contact-centre and back-office agents working from home need their CRM and contact-centre applications without installing or managing them on a personal device, GSM-quality voice over home internet, protection for the customer data agents can see, an audit trail for productivity, and a fixed IP address per agent to satisfy DoT rules.
key_outcomes: Split architecture: contact-centre applications are delivered on virtual desktops, while the VoIP softphone runs locally on the agent's own machine and reaches the voice system (Avaya, Aspect, Cisco, Genesys) through the access gateway

Accops Turbo is a UDP-tunnelled private-access technology built on the Noise protocol framework, Curve25519, ChaCha20, Poly1305, BLAKE2, SipHash24 and HKDF, intended for low-bandwidth links with high packet loss

Turbo assigns a unique static virtual IP address to the agent at every login, bound to a virtual adaptor on the device and either NATed at the HySecure gateway or routed internally - the mechanism the deck offers for DoT compliance
Device trust: domain-join, geolocation and movement tracking, MAC and hardware-signature checks, plus device health checks for anti-virus, firewall, Windows update, browser and OS version

Data copy-protection: blocks copy-paste, print-screen, screen recording, file download, printing and USB; endpoint control can block internet and run in stealth or always-on mode; daily, weekly and monthly productivity and access reports

A 14-row comparison table against 'Other VPNs' and 'Other VDI Solutions' - no vendor is named in it - covering VoIP performance, device and credential sharing, BYOD, fixed IP, watermarking and screen-capture blocking
Case study: a bank's five contact centres on an Ameyo Android softphone, with Accops securing traffic from the mobile app to the Ameyo VoIP server so agents cannot log in from multiple devices
Licensing: subscription or perpetual, named or concurrent users, with 24x7 technical support
cards.brief: A 14-slide pandemic-era industry deck for BPO, KPO and contact-centre operators, marked 'ACCOPS CONFIDENTIAL' on the title slide. It opens with the business case for home working and its risks, sets out what the organisation and the agent each need, then presents the architecture that separates application delivery (virtual desktops) from voice (a local softphone through the HySecure Turbo tunnel). Two slides explain Turbo's cryptography and its fixed virtual IP, a third ('Accops Turbo Performance') is a chart image whose throughput and latency figures are not in the extracted text - read the slide before quoting any number. It closes with Digital Workspace controls, the comparison table, a two-slide bank contact-centre case and a licensing slide. The voice vendors named (Avaya, Aspect, Cisco, Genesys, Ameyo) are the incumbent systems Accops sits alongside, not displacement targets. This v4 is a trimmed deck: unlike the carded v3 PDF it carries no company-profile, customer-list or Nano secure-USB slides.
cards.use_for: A BPO, KPO, contact-centre or bank call-centre prospect asking how agents can work from home with a softphone, a fixed IP for DoT compliance and no customer data left on the home PC. The shortest version of the Turbo VoIP tunnel explanation, and the one to use when you want the solution story without the corporate-profile padding.
cards.stale_risk: The body carries no date; 2020 is inferred from the Coronavirus-pandemic framing and from the matching v3 edition, which is stamped 2020. The PowerPoint file properties are misleading in both directions - the file was created in January 2019 from a 'Zero Trust Networks' template and re-saved on 14 October 2026, so neither date describes the content. DoT OSP rules for work-from-home were relaxed in 2020-21, so check whether the static-IP requirement the deck is built around still applies before leading with it. 'Accops DPAN technology' on the benefits slide appears to be a legacy name for Turbo.
cards.internal_reason: Title slide is marked 'ACCOPS CONFIDENTIAL'; no verified public URL.

cards.title: Securing End User Computing in the AI Era - Nutanix .Next 2026 Australia Session (V1.0, 29 Slides): AI-Accelerated Exploitation, the Six-Block Accops Platform, HyDesk Hardware Table and the Nutanix Alliance
cards.client: An anonymised 'largest customers' slide (an Indian federal government IT division, the world's 7th largest life insurer, India's largest e-commerce company, the UK's largest TPA, the 3rd largest private bank, Japan's 5th largest university, India's largest company, a large Indian securities firm, India's largest bank, the world's 2nd largest service provider) with user counts; a sector-grouped reference-customer logo wall (banks, financial services, education, healthcare, pharma, government); plus two named-in-text use cases - global L&D labs at 6,000+ concurrent users per lab, and 350,000 employees on client-provided laptops needing private-app access
cards.client_actual: JioPC is the only customer named in the text (slide 12): converting TVs and set-top boxes into virtual PCs for 1.6 million users. Every other customer is anonymised by the deck itself; the logo wall on slide 15 is images and carries no extractable names.
cards.key_problem: AI has made vulnerability discovery and exploitation fast enough that patching alone cannot keep up, while the tools enterprises rely on each have a structural blind spot - EDR misses polymorphic in-memory malware, WAFs wait for signatures, SSE cannot read encapsulated traffic and physical segmentation is rigid. Meanwhile the hybrid-work stack assembled to address this has become six or more vendors with incompatible licensing, integration overhead and inconsistent policy.
key_outcomes: Threat framing: the deck cites 'Anthropic's Claude Mythos (Preview)' as evidence that AI models now surpass humans at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, giving three examples - a 27-year-old flaw that remotely crashes OpenBSD, a 16-year-old FFmpeg flaw, and a Linux-kernel privilege escalation reached by autonomously chaining multiple vulnerabilities

Sourced exposure statistics, all with citations on the slide: 86% of commercial codebases contain vulnerable open-source components and 81% of those carry high- or critical-risk flaws (Black Duck 2025); 5-15% of enterprise dependency graphs are already end-of-life (Sonatype 2026); 218 new vulnerabilities per end-of-life component every six months (Chainguard 2024)
The three-part answer the deck organises around: isolate the crown jewels, reduce the threat vector, contextualise and validate every access

A tool-landscape map placing ZTNA, SSE, Secure Enterprise Browser, IAM, VDI, UEM, Remote Browser Isolation and DEX tools against who they serve (corporate device vs BYOD, private apps vs SaaS vs internet)
The six-block Accops platform repeated as a spine through the product slides: ZTNA Gateway; IAM, MFA and SSO; Virtual Apps and Desktop; Enterprise Browser; Thin client / OS; Endpoint Management

ZTNA block: zero-trust app gateway, device posture checks, web and client-server apps, app micro-tunnels, reverse proxy, quantum-safe encryption, on-demand DLP, agent and agentless - positioned as a 'sovereign ZTNA solution' for vendor and agentless access

VDI block: session-based and personal desktops, virtual apps, Linux desktop and app, profile and user-experience management, 3D graphics, session recording, API integrations - a 'sovereign VDI stack' on any hypervisor including Red Hat OpenShift, HPE VME and Proxmox

Enterprise Browser block: privacy-enabled browser with 600+ controls, private and SaaS app access, DLP, built-in content filtering, AI-based phishing threat control, central management, built into Accops ZTNA

Accops Spectra (UEM): SaaS-based management of iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, Linux and Windows IoT / Linux thin clients; MDM, MAM and MCM; app install, upgrade and patching; digital employee experience management; proactive device-failure detection and asset management

HyDesk hardware table comparing the HY1000, HY4000 and HY6000 families on CPU, RAM, storage, OS (HyDesk Linux OS, Windows 10 IoT/Pro), ports, display, power (5W PoE-optional up to 15W), certifications (RoHS/REACH, UL, CC, IEC, EN, BIS), warranty and country of origin (UK, China, Thailand/Taiwan) - the CoO row is the one to reach for in a sovereignty or procurement conversation

Company facts: Pune HQ with a Dubai office, first product in 2016, part of the Reliance Group since September 2023, 1000+ enterprise customers, 200+ partners, 350+ team, 2M+ users served, presence across India, Japan, UAE, Saudi Arabia and seven other countries

Nutanix alliance detail: engineering-level integration and regular product certifications, Nutanix Files with FSLogix, Nutanix Flow integration, Prism integration for dynamic provisioning, shadow clone with gold master, vGPU support, one launchpad for apps and VDI; other technology partners listed are Microsoft (Gold Partner), Supermicro, Red Hat (OpenShift/OpenStack), HPE, Dell, VMware (Broadcom) and Proxmox via its Indian distributor

Use case - L&D labs: multiple global labs at 6,000+ concurrent users each, heavy IT overhead and a need to delegate provisioning, solved with ICT lab automation, self-service delegation to lab owners, on-demand per-user provisioning and lower licensing cost

Use case - private app access: 350,000 employees on client-provided laptops reaching HRMS, payroll and other private apps, replacing a remote-browser-isolation incumbent whose licensing was escalating, migrated to Accops VDI in a customer-assembled DaaS model on 100% Linux infrastructure with browser, PDF and OpenOffice support
cards.brief: A 29-slide English session deck built for a Nutanix .Next 2026 event in Australia and delivered by an Accops VP Sales (named on the title slide). It is the same 'Securing End User Computing in the AI Era' story as the Tokyo 2026 Japanese deck, rebuilt for an Australian partner audience. The arc is: an AI-era threat narrative with cited statistics, why existing tool categories fall short, a three-part answer (isolate, reduce, contextualise), the hybrid-work tool landscape and the vendor-sprawl problem, an about-us slide, then one slide per platform block, the HyDesk hardware table, partnerships, anonymised customer proof, the Nutanix alliance page, two detailed use cases, the combined Accops + Nutanix stack and a 'why Accops' close. Slide 2 produced no extractable text (image or blank) and the extraction for the largest-customers slide (16) returns the deployment descriptions and the customer descriptors as two separate blocks, so the pairing of a given user count to a given customer is not reliable from the text - open the slide before quoting any specific pairing. Most slides carry a '© 2026 Accops' line.
cards.use_for: A Nutanix partner or joint prospect in Australia or any English-speaking market, and more generally any 2026 conversation that needs the AI-era security framing with real citations behind it. The strongest current source for the six-block platform story in one place, for the HyDesk hardware comparison including country of origin, and for the Nutanix integration specifics (Files with FSLogix, Flow, Prism provisioning, vGPU, shadow clone). The L&D lab and 350,000-user private-app cases are the two proof points to lead with.
cards.stale_risk: The deck contradicts itself on Gartner recognition: the about-us slide (9) says 'In 2023 & 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant, as well as 2023 Market Guide for DaaS', while slide 13 claims 'Two Consecutive Years in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for DaaS 2026 & 2025'. One of the two is wrong and both are in the same deck - settle it before presenting. The title slide also misspells the country as 'Autralia'. The 'Anthropic's Claude Mythos (Preview)' attribution on slide 3 is a third-party AI product claim that has not been verified here. JioPC is given as 1.6 million users, where other Accops material has been noted as saying 18 million.
cards.internal_reason: Unreleased event deck with an anonymised install-base slide and partner-confidential integration detail; no verified public URL.
